summary: Yakima County, WA: a two-story L-4 cab built in 1934 above Bumping Lake, removed or destroyed in 1972; garage foundations and a few unidentified foundation parts are described on the drive-up summit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says removed in 1972; firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed in 1972. Same event, different verb; the story reports both.
The register and the July 19, 1934 roof photographs fit 1934; Willhite cites an inventory that dates the tower 1933 to 1934. The story gives 1934 as the register's date and notes the range.
The register and firelookout.com name the Wenatchee National Forest; Forest Lookouts and Willhite's 1944 account name the Snoqualmie National Forest. Left unresolved in the story.

notes_for_editor: Two different Miners Ridge lookouts exist. The Snohomish County tower near Glacier Peak (firelookout.com/wa/minersridge.html, built 1953, volunteer-staffed) is standing and is NOT this record; keep them apart on the map. Location conflict: FFLOS gives 46.80267, -121.36295 and West US Lookouts gives 46.80889, -121.35444, about 1 km apart; the story does not depend on which is the summit. The 1944 women's team account is quoted from a Joan Burton article reproduced on Willhite's page; the original publisher was not identified. No photos added: the 1934 panoramas are credited to the National Archives (Pacific Northwest Region) on FFLOS, but no image URL was retrieved.
